chunks: And among them is Ayyub ibn Nuh ibn Darraj:

key_terms.أَيُّوبُ بْنُ نُوحٍ: Ayyub ibn Nuh, a specific narrator and emissary
key_terms.إِمَام: Imam, the religious and political leader in Shia Islam
key_terms.دَرَّاجٌ: Darraj, the father or grandfather's name indicating lineage

ai.seo_question: Who is Ayyub ibn Nuh ibn Darraj in Shia Islamic history?
ai.summary: Ayyub ibn Nuh ibn Darraj is listed among the four prominent deputies (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'ah) of Imam al-Mahdi (aj) during the Major Occultation, serving as a crucial link in the chain of transmission for Shia jurisprudence. His inclusion in Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the institutional continuity of the Imamate through appointed emissaries who guided the community in the absence of the Twelfth Imam.
